blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ Dislikes Telling People what would Displease them

Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ was once displeased when he saw some Sufrah (a fragrance usually worn by women that stains the clothing yellow) on a person. After the person had left, Rasulullaah ﷺ said (to the other Sahabah (RA)), "Why do you people not instruct him to wash the Sufrah off?" Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "It was never the habit of Rasulullaah ﷺ to tell a person on his face something that would displease him."[^2]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Whenever the news reached Rasulullaah ﷺ that someone had said something, he would never say, 'What is the matter with that person to say...?' He would rather say, 'What is the matter with some people who say...?'
The Statement of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) Concerning His Modesty with his Wives
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) said, "I have never seen the private parts of Rasulullaah ﷺ."[^3]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Statement about the Modesty of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ's wife Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) both reported to him that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) once sought permission to see Rasulullaah ﷺ who was lying down on his bed wearing a shawl belonging to Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA). Remaining as he was, Rasulullaah ﷺ permitted Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in and he left after completing the work he had with Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ was still in the same condition when Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked permission to enter. Rasulullaah ﷺ allowed him in and after completing his work with Rasulullaah ﷺ, Hadhrat Umar (RA) also left. However, when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) sought permission to enter, Rasulullaah ﷺ sat up and urgently asked Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) to ensure that her clothes were covering her properly. After Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) had completed the work he had with Rasulullaah ﷺ, he then also left.
Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) then asked, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Why is it that you became more anxious at the arrival of Uthmaan (RA) than you did at the arrival of both Abu Bakr (RA) and Umar (RA)?" Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "Uthmaan (RA) is extremely bashful and I feared that if I let him under the condition that prevailed, he would have been unable to fulfil the need he had
Bazzaar. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.17) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Ahmad. Nasa'ee in his "Yowm wal Layl" and Abu Dawood have also reported the narration.
